scenes.headline: Data Plane
scenes.subtitle: Where your compute and data actually live
scenes.narration: The data plane is the compute layer inside your own cloud account where Spark clusters process your data.

scenes.headline: What the data plane does
items: Runs cluster worker and driver VMs in your cloud subscription
Reads and writes directly to your object storage
Executes all Spark transformations and queries
scenes.narration: The data plane provisions the virtual machines that form your clusters. Those nodes talk straight to your object storage such as S3 or ADLS. All heavy computation happens here, close to the data.

scenes.headline: Classic data flow
scenes.narration: Worker nodes fetch data directly from your storage buckets. Spark performs the transformations across the cluster in parallel. The results are written back to storage without routing bulk data through Databricks.

scenes.headline: Classic vs serverless data plane

columns.title: Classic
points: Full control over VPC and instances

scenes.narration: With the classic data plane, compute runs in your own account and you control the network. With serverless, Databricks hosts the compute for faster startup and less operational overhead. The trade-off is control versus convenience.

scenes.headline: Why it matters
items: Data stays within your security and residency boundary
Compute scales elastically with your workload
You control instance types and cost
scenes.narration: Because processing happens where your data lives, sensitive information never leaves your perimeter. Clusters scale up and down to match demand. You choose instance families to balance performance and cost.

scenes.text: The data plane is where the real work happens: your VMs, your storage, your data.
scenes.narration: If the control plane is the brain, the data plane is the muscle that lifts every byte of your data.
